newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Arab envoys seek Security Council meeting.
newsitem.headline: Arab envoys seek Security Council meeting.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation and Saudia Arabia, as chairman of the Arab group, have asked for a Security Council meeting to deal with violence in the Israeli-occupied territories, Arab sources said on Thursday.
They said the request was decided on at an Arab group meeting and was expected to be considered by council members during previously scheduled consultations later in the day.

The Arab group was said to be seeking the closing of an archaeological tunnel in the Old City of Jerusalem at the centre of clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops that have claimed more than 50 lives in the past two days.
It also wants the council to demand that Israel resume the Middle East peace process and abide by agreements already concluded with the Palestinian Authority, the sources said.

In response to an earlier letter from the PLO, the Security Council president in a statement on Wednesday said council members were concerned at the situation in Jerusalem and the West Bank town of Ramallah, scene of much of the initial bloodshed, and urged "all sides to move quickly to restore calm and to exercise restraint and avoid further violence."
